meta.title: Political theory knowledge network, c. 1755-2026
meta.description: Key works and debates in political theory: distributive justice and equality, ideal and nonideal theory and realism, legitimacy and public reason, deliberative democracy, representation, epistemic democracy and epistemic injustice, republicanism and domination, global justice and human rights, migration and the boundary problem, race and colonialism, feminist theory, multiculturalism and recognition, the history of political thought, critical theory and radical democracy, populism, work and the economy, and climate and intergenerational justice. Seeds come from this repo's papers.json (including the Gov Theory reading list); works shared with the other maps are imported from them; others are top-cited 2006-2026 articles selected via Crossref (including fourteen political-theory and philosophy journals) plus anchoring books and classics. Direction: source (later or dependent work) -> target (earlier or anchoring work).

edge_types.builds_on: source extends or relies on target's argument or evidence
edge_types.challenges: source contests target's claim, mechanism or evidence
edge_types.qualifies: source adds a scope condition or moderating factor to target
edge_types.extends_to_new_case: source applies target's logic to a new population, period or domain
edge_types.synthesizes: source integrates target with other work
edge_types.mechanism_tested_by: source tests a mechanism implied by target

meta.verification: Repo works come from the user's Zotero library. Works imported from the other six maps keep their verification. Crossref-selected works take title, authors, year, venue and DOI from Crossref records. Anchors are checked in Crossref separately; see each node's `verified` field. One-line claims for non-repo works are my summaries.
